newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals disappointed by Thailand.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals disappointed by Thailand.

text.p: Southeast Asian currencies remained uninspired on Wednesday, the morning after Thailand announced its long awaited economic rescue package and left the market wanting more.

The plan -- a series of tough measures aimed at cutting the current account deficit and reviving Thailand's beleaguered economy -- was applauded by Japan and the United States but dealers said it left the market largely unmoved.

Disappointment over Thailand's failure to lift capital controls imposed in mid-May and uncertainty over the amount of aid it would receive from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and other countries also dampened interest.

The Thai baht recovered some composure as the market absorbed Tuesday's news that the central bank had suspended an additional 42 finance companies, following the suspension of 16 finance firms in June.
The baht was at 31.60/31.70 to the dollar at 0435 GMT in the onshore market compared with 31.70/32.00 late on Tuesday.
The offshore rate was at 31.05/15 against 31.35/45 but Singapore dealers said there was very little trade.
"Nobody's willing to quote the Thai baht in good amounts anymore so $5 (million) can just move the market," a European bank dealer said.
Bangkok dealers said liquidity was expected to improve on an expected increase in bank deposits as customers would shift funds to commercial banks from troubled finance companies.
In Malaysia, the ringgit weakened further as players discounted news of central bank curbs on currency swap transactions and dealers said the ringgit could test recent lows.
"The dollar trend is still strong. The swaps restriction will not be effective for a while as the market is well funded," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said the market was already long on ringgit positions and offshore players accounted for the bulk of liquidity in the forward market.
The ringgit was at 2.6400/30 to the dollar at 0435 GMT after hitting a low of 2.6445 against 2.6335/85 late Tuesday.

Bank Negara ordered local banks to limit non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer from Monday as part of an effort to cool speculation in the ringgit and bring down interest rates.
"I think the dollar was oversold on Monday. Dollar/ringgit should go back to 2.6500/50 before we see it coming down again," another Singapore dealer said.
Some local companies were seen selling dollar/ringgit around 2.6440 in early trade, but the rebound was limited by talk of good-sized bids at 2.6400 from local and offshore players.
The Singapore dollar was soft after slipping back through the 1.47 level against its U.S. counterpart overnight. But dealers said its day's bottom was likely to be 1.4750.
The Indonesian rupiah firmed as higher domestic short-term rates prompted operators to unload dollars. Spot rupiah was at 2.588/95 at 0435 GMT against 2,595/605 late on Tuesday.
"Sentiment on the rupiah seems to have improved. We even see some 'good name' foreign investors looking for rupiah assets to lock in current attractive rates," a state bank dealer in Jakarta said.
He said offshore operators were starting to unload dollars but sustained local demand was limiting the U.S. unit's downside.
The Philippine peso continued to show a firm bias after opening higher as banks sold dollars to abide by the central bank's newly imposed five percent limit on long dollar positions.
The peso was at 28.55/60 to the dollar against Tuesday's 28.65 close.
Manila traders said the central bank also indicated its preference for a stronger peso by quoting an offer rate for the dollar at 28.80 on Wednesday from the previous 29.
The Taiwan dollar had a choppy morning, recovering from its opening lows on suspected central bank intervention.
But it had slipped back to around T$28.643/649 at 0435 GMT from a morning high of T$28.605 as the U.S. dollar's strength against major currencies continued to weigh on the market.
